Daniel’s “failed replication” may be less a musical mystery than a modeling mismatch: the bluesy D♯ in the original build seems to arise specifically from *multi-key interaction* in a resistor ladder—i.e., pressing two keys creates an unintended parallel path that produces a *new effective resistance* (your “1 in parallel with 1/2 gives 1/3” step). The Python search, by contrast, appears to enumerate what can be built with **N resistors as a single network**, not what emerges when **two separately-designed taps are shorted/combined by the keyboard wiring**. Those are different design spaces: a ladder with switches is closer to “a base network plus switch-induced graph rewrites,” and it can generate extra mediants-like values even when no individual key is “designed” to yield them. If Daniel wants the computation to explain the hardware surprise, the object to simulate is the *whole ladder + switching matrix*, then evaluate the resulting resistance for every subset of pressed keys (including 2-key and 3-key chords), not just every standalone network of size N.

A second blind spot is the insistence on equal temperament as the arbiter of what “counts” (“within 10 cents of ET”). Resistor networks naturally generate *rational* relations (series/parallel arithmetic), which aligns more directly with the tradition of **just intonation** (simple frequency ratios) than with 12-TET bins. The early tiers Daniel gets—C, then C–F–G—look exactly like the “3-limit” world built from primes 2 and 3 (octaves and fifths), a pattern long discussed in tuning theory and closely related to how rationals are organized by continued fractions / mediants (the [Stern–Brocot tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stern%E2%80%93Brocot_tree) is the clean mathematical reference). Blues, meanwhile, is famous for *microtonal inflection*—the “blue third” is often closer to something between minor and major third than a fixed D♯ in 12-TET—so an ET snap-to-grid filter can erase precisely the phenomenon Daniel is looking for. A more revealing output would be: list each achievable pitch as cents relative to the tonic *without* rounding to ET, then separately annotate which ones lie near culturally salient “blue” regions (and, if desired, compare to just ratios discussed in works like Partch’s [*Genesis of a Music*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genesis_of_a_Music) rather than to 12-TET note names).
